# API reference customisation

Add project-specific notes, change docstring sections or select renderer subclasses
while Great Docs generates an API reference. An extension can customise each
object, including methods embedded in a class page and objects sharing one page.

Use semantic hooks for documentation that should also appear in `llms-full.txt`.
Use renderer methods for changes to the generated pages.

## A note on each object

Configure a Python entry file relative to the selected `great-docs.yml`:

```{.yaml filename="docs/great-docs.yml"}
api_reference_extension: _api_reference_extension.py
```

Create that file with a callable `setup(extension)`:

```{.python filename="docs/_api_reference_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.pandoc.blocks import BlockContent, Blocks, Para
from great_docs.rendering import Renderers


class AppendNoteMixin:
    def render_docstring_body(self) -> BlockContent:
        body = super().render_docstring_body()
        return Blocks([body, Para("Prepared for this project's documentation.")])


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(doc_mixin=AppendNoteMixin))
```

Run `great-docs build`. The note appears after the object's docstring sections
and before its member groups. Each embedded method gets its own note.

Keep `api_reference_extension: null`, the default, to use the built-in output.
The configured path may also be absolute and must name a `.py` file. Reading
configuration or authored reference sections does not execute that file.

## Semantic hooks

Register handlers through the supplied `Extension`, directly or as decorators.
Lower priorities run first; registration order breaks ties. Existing global
hook templates precede local handlers at equal priority. Registration closes
when setup finishes, including for decorators saved for later use.

| Method | Timing | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `on_object_resolved` | Before constructor-aware parsing and documentation-based member selection | Retain or replace the current object; return `None` to exclude it |
| `on_docstring_parsed` | After parsing, for objects with docstrings | Retain or replace the section list; returning `None` is invalid |

For example, select `_semantic_extension.py` as the entry file to add text that
also appears in semantic export:

```{.python filename="docs/_semantic_extension.py"}
import griffe as gf

from great_docs.extensions import Extension


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    @extension.on_object_resolved
    def add_note(obj: gf.Object | gf.Alias) -> gf.Object | gf.Alias:
        if obj.docstring is not None:
            obj.docstring.value += "\n\nThis description includes a project note."
        return obj
```

Each underlying object is prepared once per operation. Aliases share semantic
edits, parsed sections and exclusion decisions while keeping their authored
names and destinations. Edit the current object's docstring, sections or
documentation metadata. Arbitrary changes to descendants, bases, member
structure and module collections are outside this interface.

Parsing uses the operation's language and `parser` setting, including when a
helper or typing page prepares the object first. A handler that introduces a
directive may select an earlier priority when it needs to precede another
handler. The existing `great_docs.hooks` decorators remain available for
programmatic templates; configured setup must use the supplied instance.

## Appearance context

Use the renderer's `self.context` for the object's name and page. Treat the
object and settings referenced by the frozen `RenderContext` as read-only.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `obj` | The prepared object or authored alias view |
| `authored_name` | The name selected for this occurrence |
| `canonical_identity` | The underlying object's qualified identity, shared by aliases |
| `page_path` | The output-relative QMD destination, or `None` when unknown |
| `level` | The occurrence's heading depth |
| `contained` | Whether another object's documentation contains this occurrence |
| `source_root` | The original documentation source directory, or `None` when unavailable |
| `output_root` | The explicit generated-project root, or `None` outside a known build |
| `settings` | The operation's semantic and rendering settings |

Use `context.obj`, `authored_name` or `page_path` to select an appearance. Aliases
can have different names and page paths while sharing `canonical_identity`.
Contained members retain their real containing page. Programmatic helpers
without a known page receive `page_path=None`.

## Authored Usage markup

Select `_usage_extension.py` to replace an authored example within the object's
rendered body:

```{.python filename="docs/_usage_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.pandoc.blocks import BlockContent
from great_docs.rendering import Renderers


class ReplaceUsageMixin:
    def render_docstring_body(self) -> BlockContent:
        body = super().render_docstring_body()
        if body is None:
            return None
        return str(body).replace("old_usage()", "new_usage()")


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(doc_mixin=ReplaceUsageMixin))
```

This changes authored Usage content such as a fenced `old_usage()` example. The
leading subject is in the description. Use the corresponding renderer methods
to change the description, title, signature or automatic Usage row.

## Renderer selection

Select ordinary subclasses through `Renderers`. For example, select
`_signature_extension.py` to omit class signatures:

```{.python filename="docs/_signature_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.pandoc.blocks import BlockContent
from great_docs.rendering import ClassRenderer, Renderers


class QuietClass(ClassRenderer):
    def render_signature(self) -> BlockContent:
        return None


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(classes=QuietClass))
```

A source link can remain when a signature is omitted. The Usage/source row is
omitted when both the signature and source link are absent.

Select `_summary_extension.py` to change function labels in summaries:

```{.python filename="docs/_summary_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.rendering import FunctionRenderer, Renderers


class LabelledFunction(FunctionRenderer):
    @property
    def summary_name(self) -> str:
        return f"Run {super().summary_name}"


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(functions=LabelledFunction))
```

The replacement slots are `classes`, `functions`, `attributes`, `type_aliases`,
`modules`, `api_pages`, `reference_index` and `reference_sections`. Each accepts
a subclass of its corresponding supported renderer. Omitted slots use defaults.
Declaring a subclass changes no shared renderer class.

Pass `doc_mixin=YourMixin` to place a cooperative mixin before each default
object renderer. Explicit replacements control their own inheritance and must
include that mixin themselves when needed. Pages and reference sections do not
receive the object mixin.

| Method or projection | Scope |
|---|---|
| `render_title`, `render_title_content`, `title_content` | Visible headings and the object content used for page titles |
| `render_description`, `render_signature` | Subjects, signatures and their surrounding presentation |
| `render_docstring_body` | Own docstring sections, including section headings |
| `render_members_summary(kind, renderers)` | Summaries for embedded or separately documented members |
| `render_members_body(kind, renderers)` | Embedded member bodies |
| `render_body` | Full body composition, including automatic member groups |
| `render_summary`, `summary_name` | Summary entries and labels |

Return `None` from a block-rendering method to hide that content. Return an
empty sequence from `render_summary()` to omit its entries. Hiding member
presentation preserves resolved membership and inventories.
Cached projections such as `signature`, `title`, `description` and `body` call
their corresponding rendering methods. Override the methods to change their
output. Override `render_docstring_body()` to change an object's docstring sections.
Use `render_body()` to control the whole body, including member groups.

## Shared code and lifetime

Import a shared installed package from setup to reuse registrations across
projects. Its ordinary Python import cache is preserved. Import project-local
helpers relatively, for example `from ._shared import register`, to reload
current helper source for each operation. Relative imports remain available
during callbacks and are released when the operation closes.

Use `extension.cache` for project-owned state within one operation. Read
`extension.settings`, `source_root` and `config_root` as operation values. The
configuration root is the selected configuration file's parent; the source root
is the original documentation source directory, including during staged rebuilds.
Neither root is inferred from the current working directory.

Each build, semantic query or preview generation owns fresh extension state.
Setup runs once before that operation first prepares or renders documentation.
Successful completion and failures release owned imports. Closing an unused
reference does not run setup. Global templates share callback objects rather
than copying their internal state. General concurrent/interleaved operations
are outside this contract.

The `render_type_object` and `render_code_variable` helpers accept
`customisation=reference` to share an active `APIReference`. Omitted helper
settings use that reference's settings; conflicting settings raise an error.
Standalone helpers use default settings unless supplied, apply parser defaults
and own their preparation lifetime. Separate source snippets keep separate
identities even when their temporary module names match.

## Export and failures

The build reuses its prepared reference for the LLM index and full semantic
export after API generation. Semantic edits, exclusions, constructor facts,
overloads, annotations and defaults are retained. Selected renderers affect pages only.
An explicitly omitted constructor body, such as
with `members: []`, stays omitted while its class signature retains constructor
facts.

Standalone full export constructs and closes its own reference, preserving
missing/import diagnostics and valid sibling entries. It uses the selected
configuration's parser and dynamic defaults, with explicit reference settings
taking precedence.

Configured failures report the entry file, actual phase and relevant object or
occurrence, preserving their original cause. They stop the operation instead
of causing static retry or warning-only export. Preview retains the last
successful published project after a failed rebuild.

## Preview inputs and freeze

Declare data inputs during setup:

```python
extension.watch("data.txt")
extension.watch("data/*.txt")
extension.watch("examples")
```

Resolve these paths relative to the entry file, or pass absolute paths. Missing
inputs, creation/deletion, directory contents and glob membership are tracked.
Watching an input does not copy it into the generated project. Extension source,
relative helpers and declared inputs contribute to one final fingerprint on
every generated reference QMD, including typing pages and the index.

Preview selects its directories and filter once. It observes edits within that
initial coverage while rebuilding, including new relative helpers and glob
matches. Hidden files and generated output keep the ordinary exclusions. A new
input outside the initial coverage produces a restart message; stop and rerun
`great-docs build --watch` to observe it.

| Execution policy | Input-only changes |
|---|---|
| `freeze: auto` | Refresh affected execution when the fingerprint changes |
| `freeze: true` | Keep locked results until explicit refresh |
| Explicit freeze refresh | Execute current customised sources and save updated results |
| `freeze: false` | Use ordinary uncached execution |

After building once, explicitly refresh a generated page with its current path:

```bash
great-docs freeze docs/_quarto/default/reference/Document.qmd
```

Use the generated page path for your layout and reference entry.

See [Freeze](freeze.qmd) for refresh commands and [API documentation](api-documentation.qmd)
for reference membership and page placement.
